title: ChoiceDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog with MonarchRadioRow rows in a Modifier.selectableGroup() column
summary: Picking one of a few options is a MonarchDialog with a radio list as its content and a confirm action. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: When the person must choose one of two to six options before going on, and each option may need a line of description: the export format, which copy to keep.
whenNotToUse: For more options, or options that are long, use a screen or MonarchBottomSheet with a list. For a choice of actions without a confirm step use MonarchMenu. For a setting that changes at once use radio rows on the screen itself.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchRadioRow(selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, description: String? = null)

states.name: nothing chosen
states.description: Confirm is disabled until an option is selected (or start with the current value selected).

states.name: chosen
states.description: One row is selected; Confirm applies it.

states.name: disabled option
states.description: A MonarchRadioRow with enabled = false is announced as disabled and cannot be chosen.

states.name: pending
states.description: Confirm is a loading MonarchButton and dismissal is turned off while the choice is applied.

appearance: MonarchDialog in the raised background role; each option is a MonarchRadioRow with the default text role for its label and the muted text role for its description, and the strong accent role for the selected radio. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web ChoiceDialog shows radio cards with descriptions and tones, a Confirm button, pending and error states and a promise API. On Android the cards are MonarchRadioRow rows (label and description) inside MonarchDialog, and the dialog stays until the app closes it, so pending and error states fit in it. Option tones are not offered; say the consequence in the description. A promise-style call is a suspendCancellableCoroutine in the app. iOS uses the system confirmation dialog, which acts on the first tap and has no descriptions.
accessibility: The options are in a selectable group, so TalkBack reads each as a radio button with its position: "PDF, radio button, 1 of 3, selected".
Each row is one TalkBack element with a 48dp touch target that selects on a tap anywhere in it.
The selection is a filled radio, not color alone.
The dialog's title names the choice and is read first.
edgeCases: At the largest font size six options with descriptions scroll inside the dialog's content.
Keep the current value selected when the dialog edits an existing setting, so Confirm is enabled at once.
